article: Post messages to Microsoft Teams from C++ with WinHTTP and Microsoft Graph
findings: Replaced the unsupported client-credentials posting instructions with delegated ChatMessage.Send guidance; limited Chat.ReadBasic to listing chats and ChannelMessage.Send to channel posts; identified Teamwork.Migrate.All as migration-only.
Replaced the unsafe WinHTTP wide-string body with UTF-8 JSON bytes, JSON escaping, RAII handle cleanup, request error checks, and an HTTP 201 success check.
Made the device-code sample explicitly partial, added offline_access guidance for refresh tokens, and documented the optional Chat.ReadBasic scope.
Fixed duplicate date metadata while preserving the 2025-07-14 publication date, added lastmod and accurate localized descriptions, and removed unsupported attachment advice.
Compared the full Japanese article with all twelve translations, including setup, permissions, authentication, code, pagination, operational notes, summaries, terminology and references.

post/C++ から Microsoft Teams にメッセージを投稿する方.source: post/C++ から Microsoft Teams にメッセージを投稿する方法（WinHTTP + Graph API）/index.md

meaning.note: Compared the complete translation against Japanese: app registration, delegated versus application permissions, device-code sign-in limits, token scope, chat ID retrieval and pagination, posting behavior, operational notes, summary and source-article claims.

terminology.note: Checked localized terms for delegated access, client credentials, public clients, device-code flow, chat/channel messages, access/refresh tokens, UTF-8, and Microsoft Graph permission names.

mathematics.note: The article contains no mathematical derivations or formulas.

code.note: Compared the identical C++ sample and PowerShell examples across all 13 editions; reviewed WinHTTP handle cleanup, UTF-8 JSON bytes, JSON string escaping, HTTPS request construction, HTTP 201 check, and scope examples. The C++ sample was not compiled or run.

links.note: Checked the five official Microsoft Graph/Entra references for chat posting, chat listing, permissions, device-code flow, and channel posting; checked localized internal Graph/OAuth links and reciprocal language navigation.
